overall: The AG found the Community Preservation Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session on October 10 without a proper purpose, and ordered compliance and release of the unredacted minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleges the Committee entered executive session on October 10 for an improper purpose regarding the Webster Woods property.
allegations.key_passage: Since the Committee’s discussions did not relate to either litigation or the purchase, exchange, lease or value of real property, we find that the Committee entered executive session without a proper purpose on October 10.

allegations.summary: Complaint argues the Committee had no litigating position to protect and no negotiating position, since the purchase price was disclosed in the October 3 funding proposal.
allegations.key_passage: We need not decide here whether the Committee had a litigating or negotiating position to protect because we find, as a threshold matter, that the Committee’s discussions in executive session were not about litigation or the purchase or value of real property.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Publicly release the October 10 executive session minutes, without any redaction or withholding.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Committee to publicly release its October 10 executive session meeting minutes.
